lines.text: He means right.
Emotionally, we are lost.
My dear, this is the marriage. Drive.
Page twelve. That's you. One joke a year.
The first eight are my mother's.
And you wouldn't believe who.
What did you write? On my BACK, Lula?
It was the imam's brother. I wrote it down. Page six.
He laughed once. Page nine. Nobody believed us.
Lula. Write the date.
The date. And: 'He laughed. Out loud. At nothing.'
Ah, you. Sit. Lula, the young one is here. No, the other young one.
Hello. Don't ask him for directions. Ask me.
Sannu da zuwa. [Welcome.] We were just talking about you. Page twelve.
Go well. He means go right.
Thank you, my dear. I'll write it down. Not as a joke. As a fact.
You're a good listener. Rare. Lula, take notes.
That was your joke? It won't make the book. Try next year.
He said left. He means right. He always means right.
Pardon? Say it again. Slowly. For the book.
Who? There was nobody there fa. Only Lula, telling it wrong.
Yes. Write that down. No, I'll write it.
No. Lula will say yes. Ignore him.
What happened today that's worth writing down? Think. Take your time.
One joke a year. This year's? Not yet. I'm a strict editor.
Heat. Lula fans me with the book. Not that book. The other book.
Rain. It'll stop at four. Lula says three. It'll stop at four.
Careful. The book. I'm fine. The book.
Tuwo again. Lula says 'Again?' every night. Forty-one years. Write that.
A notebook. For when this one is full. Thank you.
Hm. Lula will love it. Lula loves everything.
A pencil sharpener. The good one. My dear. My dear.
Every joke is dated. Some are dated twice. Those are Lula's.
My mother started the book. Her handwriting was worse than Lula's.
At night I read Lula a page. He laughs at the same ones. Every time.
You drove us with Lula giving directions. That's courage. That's in the book.
Page twelve. That's you. One joke a year. Don't let it go to your head.
Emotionally, we are still lost. Physically, we are at the motor park.
You laughed at Lula's joke. Out of kindness. I saw. I wrote it.
What did you write? On his BACK? …I wrote it. Don't tell him.
Lula wants the escalator in the book. Not a joke. A tragedy.
You visit. Not many do. You'll be in the book. Page fifteen.
The ram story. Lula told it wrong. It was the imam's brother.
The book stayed with us through the strike. Everything else went home.
Strike. Plenty of time. Not enough jokes. Quality, not quantity.
This year's joke? I have three candidates. Only one gets in.
You check before you laugh. Good. So do I.
Lula likes you. He told me. I told him to tell you. He forgot.
Market day. I bargain. Lula agrees with the seller. Every time.
That night I made Lula write the date. His handwriting. Terrible. It's in.
The last entry that year wasn't a joke. It was true. That's allowed once.
Page nine. No. I don't talk about page nine.
After convocation, come to tea. Bring a joke. We'll judge it.
Freshers. Every year one of them says something funny. I find them.
Cup final. Lula is shouting at the wrong team. Emotionally, he's right.
Elections. I read every manifesto. One had a joke. Not a good one.
Convocation. One line each. 'They graduated.' Short. True. Funny enough.
Ramadan. Iftar on the mosque grounds. Lula carries the dates. Counts them twice.
Christmas. Our neighbours' rice is the best rice. Don't tell Mama Nkechi.
Valentine's. He bought me a pen. Forty-one years. Same pen, same joke.
Harmattan. The pages curl. I press them under the radio.
